quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. On one-way streets, drive toward the edge nearest to you.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a roundabout is ahead. Enter slowly and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you must:

options.text: Move your vehicle to the right edge of the road without leaving the pavement.
Stay in your lane and keep your speed, unless there is an emergency.
Stay in your lane and slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane and keep your speed, unless there is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane and maintain your speed while being passed. In an emergency, you can speed up, slow down, or leave the road to prevent a crash.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive a vehicle with a television screen visible to the driver.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a vehicle with a television screen that the driver can see.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane. When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle, you have enough space to safely return.

questions.question: Do not use high beam headlights in fog or mist because:

options.text: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles may not see you.
Vehicles behind you may drive too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beams reflect light back toward your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Headlights must be used:
questions.correctAnswerText: From sunset to sunrise.
questions.explanation: Use headlights from sunset to sunrise. Also use them anytime visibility is low.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points, but first yield to anything still in the intersection.

questions.question: Night driving requires more caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. Use headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press the brake and keep holding it.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out while driving, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using light braking. Do not stop on the road. Instead, pull off safely to the side.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the more impact your vehicle will have if it crashes.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, in rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn on:
questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever conditions make it hard to see other vehicles or for other drivers to see you. Always use low beam headlights when you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes if it is safe.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light has the same rules as:
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: If your power steering stops working, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with extra effort, slow down, and pull to a safe area to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with extra effort, slow down, and pull to a safe area to stop.
questions.explanation: If your power steering fails, you will need to use more force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a curve or hill because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on curves or hills because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give them space to pass safely and easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them space to pass safely and easily.
questions.explanation: When another driver wants to pass, slow down to create space in front of your vehicle. This lets them complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: This sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing without a signal. You should:

options.text: Keep a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be ready to stop if one is coming. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: Parking is illegal in many places. You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road's edge.

questions.question: There may be times when 10 mph is too fast for drivers to safely operate their vehicles.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when conditions are unsafe. Bad traffic, weather, or visibility may require you to drive as slowly as 10 miles per hour.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when driving behind a large vehicle:

options.text: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Truck, bus, and van drivers may not see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your distance behind large vehicles so you can see around them and see the road ahead.

questions.question: To improve visibility lowered by rain or fog, drivers should use their:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beam headlights reflect off these conditions and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a road with two lanes traveling in opposite directions, you should:

options.text: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, move back to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
